records.speaker: Johnnie Moore

verification.notes: The source-scoped transcript at 22:54 contains Johnnie Moore saying, in first person plural, that they are committed to building a great wall of Christian Zionism all over the world to push back antisemitism. The original episode recording preserves the clip, the Podscripts episode transcript reproduces the full wording and attribution, and a separate transcript of BBC Global News Podcast reporting independently identifies Moore and quotes the central phrase. This verifies the attributed-speech claim; it does not assess the merits of Christian Zionism.

records.text: Owens said she would characterize Charlie Kirk as having been threatened financially by both Jewish donors and Christian Zionist donors.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Look, Charlie (Charlie Kirk) was threatened. He was threatened a lot, I would say threatened financially. And I want to be clear, it wasn't just by Jewish donors, but also by Christian Zionist donors.

verification.notes: Transcript context says Owens characterized both donor groups as financial threats. Current reporting corroborates a lost $2 million Jewish donor and Kirk considering inviting Owens, while the quoted Christian Zionist message is a religious warning and no independent source establishes a financial consequence from that donor. The compound claim is therefore only partly supported.

sources.title: The Forward — Jewish donors play into all the stereotypes, Charlie Kirk wrote in leaked messages
sources.relevance: Corroborates the disclosed $2 million donor loss and Kirk considering inviting Candace; does not establish financial pressure from the Christian donor.

records.text: Owens said she thought Christian Zionism was not a religious philosophy; she compared its adherents to a cult and said they used biblical language to make threats appear heartfelt.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And I think, like I said, Christian Zionism has been put on trial this year, and I'm happy for that. I think we're all awakening and this is clearly not a religion of religious philosophy at all. They act like a cult. The behavior of them is like a cult, and it's always with this veneer of your loving Christian sister is telling you this. And you're like, why do I feel like you're going to harm me, but you are citing biblical scripture and trying to create this illusion like this is coming from the heart and it's somehow not a threat.

records.text: Christian Zionists believe Benjamin Netanyahu was sent to usher in Armageddon and bring Jesus back.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They believe this is messianic, that Bibi (Benjamin Netanyahu) was sent to usher in Armageddon. That's going to bring Jesus back.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 53:44. A significant dispensationalist strain of Christian Zionism links Israel, an end-times Armageddon, and the Second Coming of Jesus. This is not held by all Christian Zionists, and the specific claim that Netanyahu personally was 'sent' to usher it in is not a standard or universally documented belief.

sources.title: Christian Zionism and its apocalyptic foundations - Ecumenical Review
sources.relevance: Supports the documented dispensationalist Christian Zionist link among Israel, apocalyptic prophecy, and the Second Coming; the statement overgeneralizes all Christian Zionists and Netanyahu's personal role.
